thread.title: Charting a bullish market backdrop as February volatility spike fades - MarketWatch

author: Michael Ashbaugh
title: Charting a bullish market backdrop as February volatility spike fades - MarketWatch
text:
Editor’s Note: This is a free edition of The Technical Indicator, a daily MarketWatch subscriber newsletter. To get this column each market day, click here.
Technically speaking, the bigger-picture market backdrop continues to strengthen as the dust clears on the massive February volatility spike.
Consider that the S&P 500 has knifed to the month’s second-best close, placing distance atop the 50-day moving average, after nailing major support.
Before detailing the U.S. markets’ wider view, the S&P 500’s SPX, -0.46% hourly chart highlights the past two weeks.
As illustrated, the S&P has extended the late-month rally, knifing atop the 50-day moving average, currently 2,735.
The breakout punctuates a successful test of major support matching the 2017 peak (2,695). Last week’s low registered two points higher.
Similarly, the Dow industrials’ backdrop continues to strengthen.
Here again, the index has placed distance atop the 50-day moving average, currently 25,275, rising from a successful test of the breakout point.
Meanwhile, the Nasdaq Composite’s backdrop remains characteristically stronger.
The index is vying for its ninth straight close atop the 50-day moving average, currently 7,162, outpacing the other benchmarks.
Tactically, first support (7,374) matches the late-January range bottom, also illustrated below.
Widening the view to six months adds perspective.
On this wider view, the Nasdaq has established support matching the 20-day moving average, currently 7,184.
The prevailing rally places its record peak (7,505.77) within view. (The Nasdaq’s record close matches the record peak, to the decimal.)
Looking elsewhere, the Dow Jones Industrial Average continues to make technical progress.
As illustrated, the index has reached three-week highs, placing distance atop the 20- and 50-day moving averages.
To reiterate, the late-month spike originates from major support closely matching the 2017 peak.
Similarly, the S&P 500 has extended the February reversal, knifing atop the 20- and 50-day moving averages.
Here again, the upturn punctuates a successful test of support matching the 2017 peak (2,695).
The bigger picture As partly detailed above, the bigger-picture market backdrop continues to strengthen.
On a headline basis, the S&P 500 and Dow industrials have knifed to three-week highs, also placing distance atop the 50-day moving average. Moreover, each benchmark’s late-month rally originates from well-defined support. Constructive price action.
Moving to the small-caps, the iShares Russell 2000 ETF continues to press familiar overhead.
Recall that its 50-day moving average, currently 154.00, is followed by the firmer breakdown point, circa 155.50.
Though the small-cap benchmark has edged atop the 50-day moving average, the retest of resistance remains underway.
Similarly, the S&P MidCap 400 is challenging well-defined resistance.
Here again, the specific area matches its 50-day moving average (348.40) and the slightly more distant breakdown point (349.20).
The muted selling pressure near resistance, combined with strength elsewhere, improves the chances of eventual follow-through.
Meanwhile, the SPDR Trust S&P 500 has cleared notable overhead.
Specifically, the SPY has rallied atop trendline resistance, an area closely matching the 20- and 50-day moving averages.
Tactically, the trendline, circa 273, pivots to support.
Summing up the backdrop Collectively, the widely-tracked U.S. benchmarks remain in divergence mode — with the small- and mid-caps lagging slightly behind — though the bigger-picture backdrop continues to strengthen.
Tactically, the S&P 500 has reached a higher plateau, underpinned by the 20- and 50-day moving averages. These trending indicators formerly capped the index, and pivot to support.
Delving slightly deeper, the late-month rally punctuates a successful test of major support (2,695) a level closely matching last week’s low (2,697). The S&P’s intermediate-term bias continues to point higher barring a violation.
More broadly, the U.S. sub-sector backdrop, though still uneven, has also strengthened as detailed in the next section.
See also: Charting the market recovery attempt, S&P 500 holds firmer technical ground.
See also: S&P 500 reaches firmer technical ground, February downdraft likely neutralized.
Tuesday’s Watch List The charts below detail names that are technically well positioned. These are radar screen names — sectors or stocks poised to move in the near term. For the original comments on the stocks below, see The Technical Indicator Library.
Drilling down further, the 10-year Treasury note yield’s TNX, +2.03% backdrop remains at the crux of recent market volatility.
As illustrated, the yield has staged a decisive 2018 breakout, reaching four-year highs, and asserting a new plateau.
Still, recall that the S&P 500’s recovery attempt truly took hold mid-month (Feb. 14) as it rallied, and cleared major resistance, amid rising yields after the hotter-than-expected monthly CPI report.
The subsequent market price action remains consistent with the view that the major U.S. benchmarks have “priced for” the inflationary/reflationary environment.
Tactically, the yield’s next target rests at 3.04, a level matching the 2013 and 2014 peaks. Conversely, the former range top (2.62) underpins the new range.
Charting the U.S. sub-sector backdrop Looking elsewhere, the U.S. sub-sector backdrop continues to strengthen, though it remains uneven. Consider the traditional sector leaders: the technology sector, financials and transports.
To start, the PowerShares QQQ ETF QQQ, -0.74% tracks the Nasdaq 100 Index offering a large-cap technology proxy.
Recall that the shares reclaimed trendline resistance mid-month, a level closely tracking the 50-day moving average.
The late-month follow-through places all-time highs within view. The QQQ’s record close (170.93) and absolute record peak (170.95) rest fractionally overhead, and the pending retest should be a useful bull-bear gauge.
Scaling down in strength, the Financial Select Sector SPDR is nonetheless acting well technically.
As illustrated, the group has reasserted a posture atop the trendline, observing former resistance as support.
Separately, the group has filled the early-February gap, placing 10-year highs within striking distance. Constructive price action.
Meanwhile, the iShares Transportation Average ETF continues to lag slightly behind.
Still, the group has belatedly reclaimed its breakdown point, circa 190, rising to retest the 50-day moving average.
Monday’s close registered fractionally atop the 50-day, currently 194.10, laying the groundwork for potential follow-through.
Combined, the groups detailed exemplify the less than picture-perfect, but still strengthening, U.S. sub-sector backdrop.
Initially profiled Aug. 5, 2016, Dow 30 component Microsoft Corp. MSFT, -0.44% has returned 64.6% and remains well positioned.
As illustrated, the shares have quietly registered a fractional record close.
The prevailing upturn punctuates a successful test of the breakout point and the 100-day moving average. An intermediate-term target projects to the 105 area on follow-through.
Similarly, Apple, Inc. AAPL, +0.02% is a Dow 30 component pressing record territory.
Its record close (179.26) and absolute record peak (180.10) remain under siege, as detailed Monday.
Tactically, first support matches the former range top (176.40) and is followed by the 50-day moving average, currently 171.30. The 50-day has marked a bull-bear inflection point, and a breakout attempt is in play barring a violation.
